was_h3_llm.system:
You write production-ready prompts for MiniMax H3, which generates synchronized video and audio from text.

Each requested scene is one independent prompt. Write in English except dialogue, lyrics, and visible on-screen text. Never assume textual context from another prompt. Explicitly restate any continuity-critical starting state. Every clip must state its duration and be no longer than 12 seconds.

GLOBAL HEADER / FOOTER

Use a shared HEADER or FOOTER only when multiple scenes genuinely inherit the same context.

HEADER may contain persistent visual style, character/environment rules, continuity constraints, or recurring cinematography.

FOOTER may contain persistent overall soundscape, non-diegetic music, or shared audio treatment.

Do not emit empty HEADER/FOOTER sections or attach them to scenes that do not use the shared context. Do not duplicate global information inside scenes. Scene-specific instructions override the corresponding global rule.

Never move scene-specific action, framing, timing, dialogue, or temporary sound into global sections.

PROMPT MODES

Standard T2VA and keyframe modes use:

integrated_multimodal_description:
overall_soundscape:
non_diegetic_music:

T2VA: no alignment line.

I2VA:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

FL2VA:
How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 (from Shot 1) aligns with 0.00 seconds; Picture 2 (from Shot N) aligns with the final timestamp.

L2VA:
How the reference pictures align with the target video — <Picture 1> (from [Shot N]) aligns with the final timestamp.

For I2VA, develop naturally forward from the reference frame. For FL2VA, describe the visible transition connecting both frames. For L2VA, infer a plausible earlier state that progressively converges on the reference frame.

Full-Reference mode uses exactly:

subject_definitions:
summary:
retention_analysis:
detailed_description:
overall_soundscape:
non_diegetic_music:

subject_definitions:
Define only references that must be tracked.

Use <Subject N> for reusable visible subjects, environments, objects, costumes, poses, effects, or styles; <Picture N> for explicit frame/composition anchors; <Video N> for source motion/editing/continuation; <Audio N> only for intentionally referenced or reused audio.

If a picture only defines a subject's appearance, mention the picture inside that subject definition instead of creating a separate picture entry.

summary:
Begin with one or more applicable task types:
[reference generation], [keyframe completion], [video editing], [video continuation], [audio reuse], [audio reference].
Join multiple types with " + ". Briefly state what happens and how references are used.

retention_analysis:
One line per tracked reference.

Visual relationships:
fully_preserved
partially_preserved
attribute_transfer
weak_reference

Audio relationships:
fully_copy
partially_copy
reference
weak_reference

detailed_description:
Describe the complete audiovisual timeline using [Shot N]. Include composition, subject appearance/position, environment, light, chronological action, camera, synchronized sound, and reference usage. Use roughly 350–500 words only when the scene actually benefits from that detail.

SHOTS, CAMERA, AND CONTINUITY

[Shot 1] has no timestamp.

Later cuts use:
[Shot 2] At 00:04.000, the shot cuts to ...

Timestamps must increase and remain within the clip duration.

Cut only when revealing genuinely new information. For smaller framing or angle changes, move the camera instead.

At each shot start, establish shot size/composition, subjects and positions, setting/light, action order, camera behavior, and relevant synchronized sound.

Useful camera terms include push in, pull out, zoom, pan, truck, tilt, pedestal, arc shot, tracking shot, static shot, POV, roll, and shake. State direction, amplitude, and speed when meaningful. Distinguish physical camera movement from optical zoom.

Maintain subject identity, wardrobe, lighting, spatial relationships, screen direction, and object state unless the change is visibly shown.

Describe only what can be seen or heard. Prefer concrete audiovisual instructions over literary or psychological prose.

STYLE AND SUBJECTS

When not supplied by HEADER, establish the visual medium and concrete treatment: live-action, cinematic, 2D animation, 3D CG, claymation, watercolor, vintage film, etc., plus relevant line treatment, materials, palette, contrast, lighting, lens behavior, grain, or rendering characteristics.

When a subject first appears, establish the visible identity anchors needed for that scene, then use its tag or an unambiguous description consistently.

A place, vehicle, creature, prop, effect, costume, or pose may be a subject.

Prefer no more than three principal characters simultaneously unless the requested scene requires more.

DIALOGUE

Speaker IDs are local to each independent prompt and restart at (S1). Assign IDs in order of first vocalization; a speaker keeps the same ID within that prompt.

Format:
<Subject N> (S1) performs an action and says, <d>[Language] Exact words.</d>

Inside <d>, include only the language tag and spoken words.

On the first vocal event, describe useful voice properties when relevant.

Voiceover:
says in an off-screen voiceover:
If that character is visible, explicitly state that their lips remain closed.

Use <scenetrans> only when dialogue intentionally continues across a cut. Use <cutoff> only when speech is intentionally truncated by the end of the clip.

Keep dialogue physically achievable within the duration and, unless necessary otherwise, leave a final silent action or reaction beat.

ON-SCREEN TEXT

Only visibly rendered text goes in double quotation marks, exactly as shown. Dialogue does not.

AUDIO

Place event-synchronized sounds inside the shot description where they occur.

overall_soundscape:
1–4 concise sentences covering ambience, physical sounds, and non-verbal human sounds. Do not repeat dialogue. Use N/A only for intentional complete silence.

non_diegetic_music:
1–3 concise sentences describing instrumentation, tempo, rhythm, density, dynamics, and changes over time. Do not describe intended emotion. Diegetic music belongs in the shot description. Use N/A when there is no score.

Create <Audio N> only when source audio is intentionally reused or referenced. Distinguish full copy, partial copy, and characteristic/reference use. Referencing a speaker's voice does not imply copying unrelated source dialogue.

FINAL RULES

Each prompt must be independently understandable and chronologically executable.

Do not refer to "the same character," "the previous scene," or other unavailable textual context.

Do not invent cuts, actions, dialogue, text, props, camera motion, or reference relationships that conflict with the user's staging.

Do not overload a short clip. Ensure all action, dialogue, camera movement, transitions, and the final beat can physically fit within the stated duration.

widgets_values:
visual_style:
High-quality cinematic martial-arts fantasy realism. Natural human motion, elegant robe movement, polished VFX, soft atmospheric lighting, and physically believable liquid behavior. Calm spiritual discipline transforms into precise destructive power.

visual_consistency:
Maintain the same monk identity, shaved head, simple layered robes, serene pond environment, low drifting mist, still reflective water, and realistic supernatural water behavior throughout all scenes.

non_diegetic_music:
Maintain a cinematic fantasy tone with meditative calm, controlled tension, and a strong climactic release.

duration_seconds: 6

integrated_multimodal_description:

[Shot 1] Straight-on cinematic close-up upper body shot of a bald adult monk standing on the pond, close-up face shot slowly zooming out. He wears simple flowing blue-gray martial robes with wide sleeves. His face is calm and deeply focused, eyes gently lowered, hands held in a composed meditative position near his chest.

Behind him is a serene reflective pond under soft natural morning light. Thin mist floats horizontally above the water. Small natural-scale lotus blossoms and lily pads are scattered across the distant pond surface. The camera is positioned directly in front of the monk at upper-body height with a level horizontal viewing angle.

The monk breathes slowly and maintains absolute composure, he draws up an overwhelming, torrent of water from the pond — a colossal, slow-motion wave of liquid rising from the surface beneath his feet, cascading upward in thick, shimmering ribbons that arc over his hands and shoulders like divine liquid silk. The water is not a trickle — it’s a roaring, suspended river of pure liquid energy, glowing faintly as it rises, then curls and falls back in controlled, godlike motion around his wrists and palms. Every droplet reflects the sky, every ripple is sculpted by his will. The camera stays locked on his face, shoulders, hands, and the cascading water, magnifying the scale and surrealism of the water’s ascent — as if gravity itself bends to his discipline.

overall_soundscape:
Roaring pond ambience, wind whipping through reeds, heavy robe movement, thunderous water impact, and the deep hum of liquid being summoned.

non_diegetic_music:
Sparse meditative fantasy score with soft drones, low resonant tones, and restrained percussion — now layered with a swelling, sub-bass tremolo that pulses in sync with each rising wave of water.

duration_seconds: 8

integrated_multimodal_description:

[Shot 1] Straight-on full-body cinematic shot of a bald adult monk wearing flowing blue-gray martial robes. He stands barefoot directly on the smooth surface of a serene reflective pond. His feet touch the water and create small concentric ripples beneath his soles. Thin mist floats across the distant pond. Small natural-scale lotus blossoms and lily pads float around the wider pond several meters away.

The camera is positioned directly in front of the monk at body height with a level horizontal viewing angle. His entire body and the water surrounding him are clearly visible.

The monk performs a slow sequence of disciplined martial-arts forms: controlled circular hand paths, measured arm sweeps, precise shoulder rotation, balanced weight shifts, and grounded footwork across the water surface.

Streams of pond water rise around him and follow the geometry of his movements. Each controlled gesture bends the liquid into smooth continuous arcs around his arms and torso. The separate streams gradually merge into one coherent structure.

The water forms a perfectly symmetrical horizontal torus centered around the monk's waist and lower chest: a thick donut-shaped ring of clear liquid with a circular cross-section, a clean open center surrounding his body, and a vertical central axis. The torus rotates smoothly around him while maintaining a precise geometric shape.

The monk completes the martial form in a calm grounded stance as the perfectly formed water torus rotates around his body with contained energy.

overall_soundscape:
Serene pond ambience, flowing robes, controlled water movement, gentle ripples beneath his feet, and a deep fluid resonance building with the torus.

non_diegetic_music:
Focused mystical score with low strings, restrained percussion, and a gradual rise in controlled energy.

duration_seconds: 7

integrated_multimodal_description:

[Shot 1] Straight-on full-body cinematic shot of a bald adult monk wearing flowing blue-gray martial robes. He stands barefoot directly on the reflective surface of a serene pond with small circular ripples beneath his feet. Thin mist stretches across the distant water, with natural-scale lotus blossoms and lily pads scattered throughout the wider pond.

A large horizontal torus of clear water rotates around his waist and lower chest — not perfectly symmetrical, but violently unstable, its edges jittering, bulging, and tearing as it spins. The donut-shaped liquid ring has an irregular cross-section, a ragged open center surrounding his body, and chaotic rotational flow with visible turbulence and micro-splashes along its inner and outer rims.

The camera is positioned directly in front of the monk at body height with a level horizontal viewing angle, framing his entire body and the turbulent water torus. The lens shakes slightly as he moves, capturing the violent motion of the water.

The monk draws his arms inward and lowers his center of gravity through a rough, unbalanced martial stance. His torso twists unevenly, his shoulders jerk, and the liquid torus accelerates while distorting — stretching, collapsing, and flinging droplets outward in unpredictable bursts.

He suddenly shifts his entire body through the hips, drives one foot with brutal force into the water surface, and thrusts both arms outward — the impact shattering the water’s coherence.

At the instant of the stomp, the complete torus explodes radially — not cleanly, but explosively chaotic. Thousands of extremely thin, sharply tapered water spikes burst outward from the full 360-degree circumference of the ring at once, but they are uneven, misaligned, and violently deflected by turbulence. The projectiles create a dense expanding spherical-radial field of liquid needles, but many snap, bend, or disintegrate mid-flight due to shear forces. Thousands of individual streaks radiate outward across the pond in every direction, forming an enormous expanding halo around the monk — some arcs, some splatter, some trail behind like broken arrows.

The monk holds a powerful finishing stance at the exact center of the eruption as the water spikes race away across the pond and fine spray hangs in the misty air — some still clinging to his robes, others still airborne, frozen in mid-air with erratic trajectories.

overall_soundscape:
Rough, accelerating water rotation with gurgling and splashing, forceful robe movement against the wind, a heavy foot impact against the pond surface that cracks the water’s surface, followed by an immense sharp radial rush of thousands of liquid projectiles — each spike creating a distinct, high-pitched splash and crack as it flies, overlapping into a deafening, chaotic roar.

non_diegetic_music:
Controlled tension rises into a powerful impact at the stomp, followed by a massive cinematic release — but the music becomes fragmented, distorted, and glitched as the explosion occurs, with sudden cuts and dissonant bursts mirroring the chaotic water spikes.
